1000:0302.name: rtl_lxmul
1000:0302.note: Borland RTL 32-bit multiply: DX:AX * CX:BX -> DX:AX (low 32 bits)

1000:033a.name: rtl_scopy
1000:033a.note: Borland RTL far struct copy: CX bytes from far [BP+6] to far [BP+0xa], callee pops 8

1000:0488.name: rtl_lxlsh
1000:0488.note: Borland RTL 32-bit shift left of DX:AX by CL

1000:04a9.name: rtl_lxrsh
1000:04a9.note: Borland RTL 32-bit arithmetic shift right of DX:AX by CL

1000:04c9.name: rtl_lxursh
1000:04c9.note: Borland RTL 32-bit logical shift right of DX:AX by CL

1008:0000.name: platform_winMain
1008:0000.note: WinMain: /c opens the config dialog, /s runs the saver, any other arg shows dialog 0x6d and then runs; registers the window class, creates a full-screen window, posts WM_USER, runs the message loop

1008:0221.name: platform_defScreenSaverProc
1008:0221.note: Default message handling: mouse move over 3 px, clicks, key down, or deactivation request exit; WM_DESTROY posts quit; then DefWindowProc

1008:0c5c.name: platform_loadSettings
1008:0c5c.note: Reads all SCRANTIC.INI keys (Background, Clouds, Waves, Sounds, NumDays, CurrentYear, StartTime, ...) into globals

1008:0dc8.name: platform_saveSettings
1008:0dc8.note: Writes the same SCRANTIC.INI keys back with WritePrivateProfileString

1008:0fcd.name: platform_screenSaverProc
1008:0fcd.note: Exported window procedure: create loads settings and starts a 50 ms timer, destroy saves settings, paint blits the offscreen image, timer runs timer callbacks and the idle callback, WM_USER checks free memory then runs init

1008:12eb.name: platform_setDialogStartTime
1008:12eb.note: Normalizes an HHMM start time (wraps at 24:00 with a beep, snaps to :00 or :30), stores it, and shows it in dialog item 0x6e

1008:13cd.name: platform_pumpInputMessage
1008:13cd.note: Peeks one pending keyboard or mouse message and dispatches it, with a busy flag set meanwhile

1008:143c.name: platform_initSaver
1008:143c.note: Startup: reads RESOURCE.MAP, sets 640x480, loads JOHNCAST.PAL, shows INTRO.SCR, registers a timer callback, draws the island, loads JOHNWALK, sets the cleanup and idle callbacks

1008:15c8.name: story_idleTick
1008:15c8.note: Idle callback: runs one scene step, then updates elapsed-time counters from GetCurrentTime

1010:0136.name: story_drawIsland
1010:0136.note: First call loads HOLIDAY.BMP, BACKGRND.BMP, MRAFT.BMP; later calls draw the background (NIGHT.SCR, a random OCEAN0x.SCR from table 1068:0262, or a fill), place the island, and set up clouds and waves

1018:0000.name: walk_loadJohnWalkBmp
1018:0000.note: Loads JOHNWALK.BMP once and resets three walk-state globals

1018:06bf.name: story_stepScene
1018:06bf.note: One scene step: when the scene queue is empty builds a new one and logs New Scene; otherwise loads the entry's ADS by id and runs its tag

1018:0c62.name: ads_loadAdsById
1018:0c62.note: Looks up an ADS id in the table at 1068:166e, unloads the previous ADS when the id changes, loads and caches the file; id -2 loads from a buffer at 1068:361c

1018:1771.name: resources_readResourceMap
1018:1771.note: Reads RESOURCE.MAP once: header, then per archive a 13-byte name and a list of 8-byte entries into a table at 1068:3365

1018:1da8.name: platform_messageBoxFromResource
1018:1da8.note: Loads a string resource, formats it with the varargs, beeps, and shows a MessageBox

1020:0000.name: audio_loadWaveResources
1020:0000.note: If Sounds is on, finds, loads, and locks the WAVESFX1..WAVESFX25 resources into a table

1020:0085.name: audio_closeMciDevice
1020:0085.note: If Sounds is on and an MCI device is open, sends MCI_CLOSE and clears the device id

1020:00ba.name: audio_playSound
1020:00ba.note: Plays WAVESFX sample 1..25 from memory with sndPlaySound when Sounds is on

1020:019c.name: platform_requestExit
1020:019c.note: Guarded exit: optional password dialog, then sends WM_CLOSE to the main window, or beeps on a wrong password

1020:0512.name: gfx_wipeEllipseOut
1020:0512.note: Transition: draws growing ellipses from the rect center, pumping input after each step

1020:05a0.name: gfx_wipeRectOut
1020:05a0.note: Transition: draws growing rectangles from the rect center, pumping input after each step

1020:0637.name: gfx_wipeRightToLeft
1020:0637.note: Transition: fills the rect in 1/100-width strips from right to left

1020:0688.name: gfx_wipeLeftToRight
1020:0688.note: Transition: fills the rect in 1/100-width strips from left to right

1020:06d2.name: gfx_wipeTopToBottom
1020:06d2.note: Transition: fills the rect in 1/200-height strips from top to bottom

1020:071c.name: gfx_wipeBottomToTop
1020:071c.note: Transition: fills the rect in 1/200-height strips from bottom to top

1020:081c.name: platform_debugLog
1020:081c.note: Printf-style debug log; empty in this build (only returns DS)

1030:01c4.name: gfx_saveRectBits
1030:01c4.note: Copies a rect of the DC at 1068:1eb6 into a caller buffer with GetBitmapBits

1030:0250.name: gfx_restoreRectBits
1030:0250.note: Puts a caller buffer back with SetBitmapBits, blits it to the DC at 1068:1eb8, marks the rect dirty

1030:02ef.name: gfx_drawLine
1030:02ef.note: Draws a line in the foreground color and marks it dirty; dirty width is wrong when x2 < x1 or y2 < y1 (uses -a-b, not a-b)

1030:082c.name: platform_registerCursor
1030:082c.note: Adds a cursor of kind 0x1111, 0x2222, or 0x3333 to a growable global table; -1 and -2 mean the system arrow and wait cursors

1030:09d0.name: platform_removeCursor
1030:09d0.note: Removes a cursor from the table; 0x4444 resets the active cursor and frees the whole table

1030:0a8a.name: platform_setActiveCursor
1030:0a8a.note: Activates a table cursor; kind 0x3333 hides the system cursor, clips it to the window, and draws a software cursor

1030:1112.name: decoders_readBmpInfo
1030:1112.note: Seeks BMP:INF:, reads the image count, allocates 14-byte records, and reads every width then every height

1030:124a.name: decoders_loadBmp
1030:124a.note: Loads a BMP resource: info via BMP:INF:, pixel data from BMP:BIN:, optional BMP:VGA: or BMP:AMG: layer; returns a handle or 0

1030:16d8.name: decoders_loadScreen
1030:16d8.note: Loads a SCR resource: size from SCR:DIM: (default 320x200), SCR:BIN: decoded in strips, optional SCR:VGA: or SCR:AMG: layer

1038:1bd8.name: gfx_drawRect
1038:1bd8.note: Draws a rect: outline when fill is off or the rect is under 2 px, else filled (PATCOPY blit when both colors match); marks it dirty

1038:1d31.name: gfx_createColorBrush
1038:1d31.note: Solid brush for colors below 16 (or in 8-color mode), otherwise an 8x8 dither pattern brush built from the two color nibbles

1040:0286.name: gfx_blitPixelRows
1040:0286.note: Turns a buffer of pixel rows into a bitmap (via 1040:0000) and blits it to the offscreen DC, marking the rect dirty

1040:0688.name: gfx_drawCircle
1040:0688.note: Draws a circle of radius r at x,y with the current pen and brush colors and marks it dirty

1040:07e6.name: platform_addTimerCallback
1040:07e6.note: Registers a far callback in a 5-slot table with an interval in base ticks

1040:089a.name: platform_runTimerCallbacks
1040:089a.note: Fires every due timer callback and advances the base tick; after a pause only resets the slot times

1040:09eb.name: decoders_loadPalette
1040:09eb.note: Takes a free palette slot (1..9), seeks PAL:VGA:, reads 16 or 256 RGB triplets through a lookup table at 1068:25b0

1040:0d54.name: gfx_drawPixel
1040:0d54.note: Sets one pixel in the given color and marks it dirty

1040:0db0.name: decoders_loadBmpMatrix
1040:0db0.note: Reads a BMP:MTX: grid of tile indices, loads the BMP tiles, and composes them into one bitmap at 1068:45f8

1040:1113.name: gfx_blitBmpMatrix
1040:1113.note: Blits a rect of the composed BMP:MTX: bitmap to the offscreen DC and marks it dirty

1048:0079.name: ads_loadAds
1048:0079.note: Loads an ADS resource into one of 10 slots: ADS:RES: id/name pairs, then the ADS:SCR: script data; returns slot + 1 or 0

1060:0a23.name: platform_globalAllocLock
1060:0a23.note: GlobalAlloc with size in DX:AX and default flags plus GMEM_MOVEABLE, then GlobalLock

1060:0a53.name: platform_globalUnlockFree
1060:0a53.note: GlobalHandle on a far pointer, then GlobalUnlock and GlobalFree
